narrative.overview:
InterviewIQ is not a SaaS dashboard; it is a courtroom deposition transcript. Every candidate answer is testimony, stamped with a line number, cross-examined against the claims on the resume. The system deliberately refuses the soft-glow, purple-gradient AI-SaaS default that shipped in the previous version of this product: no pill buttons, no glow halos, no bouncy easing. In its place is a paper/desk duality — paper-toned document panels (warm ivory, near-black ink) sit on a desk ground that goes dark or light with the ambient theme, but the paper itself never changes tone. Dashboard reads as a case docket, the live interview as a numbered transcript, and the final report as a ruling, not a scorecard.

The pairing of a serif display face for headings, a grotesque sans for UI chrome, and a true monospace for transcript/record content gives the system a documentary, procedural register — evidentiary rather than promotional. Motion is snap-decisive: buttons stamp down with a slight rotational settle, transcript lines stamp in, nothing eases softly or glows on hover.
keyCharacteristics: Paper stays paper-toned in both themes; only the desk around it goes dark/light.
One committed accent (steel blue --primary) plus one sealed-red accent (--seal) reserved for truthfulness/action emphasis — no rainbow of semantic hues beyond success/warning tied to score bands.
Near-square corners (2-4px radii) everywhere; nothing is a pill.
Real paper drop-shadows, never colored glow halos.
Monospace used structurally (transcript, timestamps, scores, badges), not decoratively.

rules.name: The Paper-Stays-Paper Rule
rules.body: --bg-surface, --bg-elevated, and --ink do not participate in the dark/light switch. Only the desk (--bg-main, --border-desk, --text-*) and the accent tones re-tune between themes. A component that inverts the paper to a dark card is off-system.

rules.name: The Sealed Red Rule
rules.body: --seal is reserved for truthfulness flags, primary case-progressing actions, and the recording state — never used as a decorative accent or applied to more than one element's worth of emphasis per view.

rules.name: The On-The-Record Rule
rules.body: Any value that is literally a recorded fact — a score, a timestamp, a status badge, a line number, a docket number — renders in Courier Prime. Prose and UI chrome never do.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow in the system carries a hue from the accent palette. Emphasis states (recording mic, selected persona, focus rings) use color-mix fills or outline/inset borders instead of a colored glow.

dos: Do keep paper (--bg-surface/--ink) identical across both themes; only re-tune the desk and accent tones.
Do use Courier Prime for anything that is a literal recorded value (scores, timestamps, badges, transcript content).
Do use .btn-seal for the action that actually commits/progresses the case (start interview, submit answer, close session) — reserve .btn-primary for lower-stakes commits.
Do shadow document panels with the neutral paper-shadow tokens; never a colored/glow shadow.
Do use the ledger-row pattern (single bordered container, hairline dividers) for any new list of like-kind entries (sessions, personas, stats) instead of a gapped card grid.
Do snap state transitions (0.12-0.28s, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) or linear) — buttons stamp with a slight rotation on press, transcript lines stamp in; nothing bounces or eases languidly.
donts: Don't invert paper to a dark surface in dark theme, or tint it toward gray/blue — it stays warm ivory.
Don't apply a colored glow/halo box-shadow anywhere; depth comes from neutral rgba(black) paper-shadows only.
Don't round any container into a pill; radii stay at 2-4px. The mic button and theme-toggle glyphs are the only intentional circles.

Don't treat the per-persona swatches (#3B6FC4 Google-blue, #A5620F Amazon-amber, plus --secondary/--primary-ink for Startup/General) as system accent tokens — they're a one-off identity-tagging palette confined to persona chips/badges, not part of the primary/secondary/tertiary accent system.
